function: Joint AP duplex-mode selection and sensing-communication beamforming (power ratio, MRT/ZF hybrid coefficient per AP) maximizing weighted sum rate plus sensing metric (pp. 7-8).
system: Cell-free network-assisted full-duplex multi-static ISAC: M=6 APs with N=4 antennas, K=6 single-antenna UEs (4 DL, 2 UL), 1 target, 250 m radius; band not stated (p. 12).
method: Hierarchical multi-agent deep RL: DDQN meta-agent selects AP modes, MADDPG agents (one per AP) set beam parameters; offline centralized training, online distributed execution (pp. 8-10).
data_channel: Custom simulator: Rayleigh fading, path-loss exponents 3.7, 3, 4, Swerling-I target RCS, random AP, UE and target positions; no standard model or public dataset (pp. 4, 12).
test_conditions: One fixed setup (M=6, N=4, K=6); tested on 500 random scenarios (Fig. 8) and 200 Monte-Carlo runs per weight mu (Fig. 9) (pp. 12, 14, 15).
baselines: Non-learned: random AP mode with MRT-CS, FPMM optimization [20]; learned: Q-learning AP mode selection with MRT-CS or ZF-CS (zeta 0.5, 0.8) (p. 14).
metrics: Communication sum rate R_com and sensing metric R_sen (log2 of 1 plus sensing SINR) as CDFs, averages and bar charts; training reward curves (pp. 7, 13-15).
complexity: Order of complexity of MAHRL inference versus exhaustive search and FPMM, with network sizes of 128 and 32 nodes per layer (Table IV, pp. 11-12).
q1_support: p. 4: "represents the small-scale fast fading"; custom Rayleigh model with path-loss exponent 3.7 (p. 12), no 3GPP, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 14: "500 randomly generated scenarios"; one setup (M=6, N=4, K=6) in Section V-A (p. 12), and Fig. 9 only varies the weight mu, which changes the reward (p. 15); no new AP, antenna or user count.
q3_support: p. 14: "Q-learning based AP mode selection and MRT-CS"; learned baseline (Q-learning, ref. [54]), with non-learned random AP mode and FPMM [20]; all compared on R_com and R_sen (Fig. 8).
q4_support: p. 11: "inference complexity between the proposed algorithm and the"; Table IV (p. 12) gives the order of complexity of MAHRL-based AMJBD, FPMM and exhaustive search.
q5_support: p. 12: "assumes a circular area with a radius R = 250"; own simulated setup, no code or data link, no public dataset.
notes: Learned part is a DDQN meta-agent plus MADDPG agents that set AP modes and per-AP beam parameters jointly, so it is physical layer (p. 8). Area 5 as ISAC beams and resources. Fig. 9 retraining per mu is implied by the mu-dependent reward, not stated (p. 15).
